chunks: What Saʿd narrated from Aḥmad and ʿAbd Allah, the two sons of Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: “Should the female slave cover her head?” He said: “No; nor is it upon the umm al-walad to cover her head if she does not have a child.”

key_terms.أُمِّ الْوَلَدِ: a slave woman who has borne a child to her master
key_terms.لَا: negation indicating the ruling of non-obligation here

ai.seo_question: Does a female slave or an umm al-walad have to cover her head in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding head-covering in salat (prayer) for a female slave and for an umm al-walad. It states that the female slave does not cover her head, and that the umm al-walad likewise does not cover her head if she does not have a child.
